outcome: Presence of SARS-CoV-2 in placental tissue
cohort: The study included five placentas from SARS-CoV-2-positive women diagnosed with mild symptoms of COVID-19 or who were asymptomatic before birth, all from term deliveries.
finding: In acute COVID-19, prominent lymphohistiocytic villitis and histopathological signs of maternal and foetal malperfusion may occur, potentially linked to SARS-CoV-2 infection of the placenta, although no transplacental transmission to the infants was observed.
